mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the past month indicates inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI increases are not followed by tighter monetary policy (FEDFUNDS unchanged or decreased).

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases are not followed by broader economic weakness (e.g., GDP growth remains strong).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 declines are not followed by broader economic weakness (e.g., strong consumer spending, RSAFS).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases are not followed by broader economic strength (e.g., GDP growth remains weak).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decreases are not followed by increased investment (e.g., weak corporate earnings growth).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals increased demand in the housing market, which typically leads to higher economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increases are not followed by broader economic strength (e.g., weak consumer spending, RSAFS).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the labor market improvements are not followed by increased consumer spending (RSAFS remains weak).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) signals increased consumer demand, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during an economic expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increases are not followed by broader economic strength (e.g., weak GDP growth, GDPC1).
